newsitem.title: USA: US stocks end sharply mixed, Dow falls 57 points.
newsitem.headline: US stocks end sharply mixed, Dow falls 57 points.

text.p: Wall Street stocks turned in a sharply mixed performance on Thursday that saw blue chips dragged lower by a stiff sell-off in tobacco shares, but technology stocks rebound from their extended slide.
The Dow industrials fell 57 points to close unofficially at 6820. Component Philip Morris Cos Inc slid 6-1/4 to 115-3/4, contributing about one-third of the average's loss.
The decline in blue chip stocks extended well beyond tobacco stocks, however, and suggested to analysts that investors were now opting to seek out bargains elsewhere.
One beneficiary was the battered tech sector, whose recent woes have produced a double-digit percentage decline in the Nasdaq Composite over the last two months weeks.
"We passed the 10 percent correction level yesterday and that seems to be a magical level that brings out the bargain hunters," said Charlie Crane, chief market strategist at Key Asset Management.
Investors also turned to the bond market, which was wobbled early by comments from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan only to rebound sharply later in the day.

Greenspan, who in testimony to Congress spoke of the need for the Fed to act "promptly - ideally pre-emptively" in its fight against inflation, heightened Wall Street's expectations for an interest rate increase at next week's Fed meeting.
However, a bond market decline has yields high enough that some now feel bonds can effectively compete with stocks.

"A lot of people think that if the Fed tightens, it's already priced into the bond market," said Roy Blumberg, chief investment strategist at Josephthal Lyon & Ross. "That makes bonds attractive, especially when you consider there's no driving inflation in the economy."

The story was far different for tobacco stocks, which toppled on news cigarette maker Liggett Group Inc was close to announcing a settlement of anti-smoking litigation with attorneys general in several states.

Sources familiar with talks between the states and Liggett, a unit of Brooke Group Ltd, said the settlement would include an offer by Liggett to turn over potentially damaging documents about the entire industry.
Shares in RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp fell 3/4 to 31-1/2 and Loews Corp, which owns Lorillard Tobacco Co, fell 2-1/4 to 98-1/2. Brooke Group rose 5/8 to 4-7/8.

In the wake of today's tumultuous session, which saw New York Stock Exchange program trading curbs imposed on three separate occasions, analysts said it would likely be some time before the market's murky outlook could clear.
Looming tomorrow is the quarterly so-called "triple witching" expiration of options, index options and index futures, an event that invariably adds volatility.
Next Tuesday, the Federal Reserve will finally begin its long-awaited interest rate policy meeting.
In the midst of it all, though, some analysts said a key measure will be whether or not the spark of life that emerged from the tech sector today gains momentum in the coming sessions.

"The techs are putting in what appears to be a pretty good bounce," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "If the techs can stabilize, the primary market won't be far behind."
In individual issues, Unisource Worldwide Inc fell 3-3/4 to 16 after warning its fiscal second quarter earnings would be below analysts' estimates.
U.S. Bancorp jumped 6-7/8 to 55-1/8 after agreeing to be acquired by First Bank System Inc for $59 per share in stock. First Bank fell 2-3/4 to 75-1/2.
The S&P 500 index fell 3.12 points to 782.65.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 9.97 points to 1259.26.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
